messages:
Mia: Heads-up, we began seeing occasional p99 jumps on streaming chat after last night's runtime change. Anyone tracking this?
Oliver: I noticed a cluster of spikes 11:10-11:30 UTC on pool-A. p95 looked fine but p99 doubled for short-turn chats.
Jasmin: I pulled traces. Tails show KV refill + a slower attention kernel used for last few tokens. Sample trace: 
perf-bot: ```
[trace] id=0x9f1a mode=stream kv_refill_ms=7.9 kv_miss=1 kernel_switched=true token_emit_ms=3.8
[latency] total=322ms service=300ms io=22ms
```
Ryan: kernel_switched=true suggests our kernel selector picked the fallback path. Did the selector threshold get tuned recently?
Mia: We adjusted kernel policy so "fast-vec" is preferred for seq>=512 earlier this week. Could that be mis-routing short-chat tails that have long prefixes?
Oliver: Also changed microbatch defaults: streaming default lowered 8->4, completions bumped 8->16. Those two changes co-occurred with the regressions.
Jasmin: My working hypothesis: smaller streaming mb reduces batching and kernel efficiency, increasing fragility to KV refills. Combined kernel fallback + refill creates long tails.
Sasha: I can run a synthetic workload (70% chat streaming, 30% non-streaming complete) against pool-A with the perf harness. Will capture kv_hit, kernel_switches, and p99.
Ryan: Include avg_batch_size in traces and a per-route kv_miss metric please.
perf-bot: test run started id=run-3021
Sasha: Baseline run (mb_stream=4, mb_complete=16, kernel_policy=auto, 10k reqs) early results: chat p95 ~92ms, p99 ~370ms, kv_miss ~3.5% in tail windows.
Mia: Can you sweep mb_stream=2,4,8,12? Interested in the knee for p95 vs p99.
Sasha: mb_stream=2 -> p95 78ms p99 540ms (kv_miss up). mb_stream=4 -> p95 92ms p99 370ms. mb_stream=8 -> p95 115ms p99 210ms. mb_stream=12 -> p95 140ms p99 190ms.
Oliver: Pattern clear: bigger mb amortizes refill cost (better p99) but increases headroom/queueing so p95 goes up. Exactly the throughput vs latency tradeoff.
Jasmin: Kernel events: with mb_stream>=8 kernel_switches drop 3x. With mb_stream<=4 they spike. Looks like kernel selector behavior depends on observed batch shape or seq distribution.
Ryan: We should consider feeding recent avg_mb and request seq_dist to the kernel selector as signals, rather than pure seq_len thresholds.
Mia: Another lever: extend prefix KV TTL for streaming sessions so refills are less frequent. But memory pressure is a concern. Can we evaluate memory cost?
Jasmin: Quick sweep of prefix_ttl: 0s, 5s, 30s. Best p99 without huge memory delta was ttl=5s + mb_stream=8. Memory delta ~6% on pool-A under our synthetic.
Sasha: Non-streaming completions (mb_complete=16) stayed stable p99 ~175-190ms across runs, so this is mainly a streaming-mode sensitivity.
Oliver: Proposed mitigation plan: 1) set streaming default mb to 6 (mode-aware default), 2) add avg_mb signal to kernel selector behind a flag, 3) short prefix_ttl bump to 5s as conservative opt.
Ryan: I'll prototype kernel selector that consumes avg_mb_1m and seq_histogram. Gate it with feature flag kernel-mb-signal for canary rollouts.
Sasha: I'll run a 10% canary on pool-A with the new defaults and flag enabled, capture p95/p99, kv_miss, kernel_switch_count. ETA 48h for runs + dashboards.
Jasmin: I will run a memory/regression check for prefix_ttl=5s across typical concurrency mix and produce an expected memory delta + GC pressure notes.
Oliver: Rollout guardrails: for tiered customers streaming p99 must stay <250ms. For canary if streaming p99 >300ms we rollback immediately.
Mia: Telemetry additions: expose kernel_switch_count, avg_mb_1m, kv_miss_rate per route in Console; add a p99-tail alert for streaming routes.
prod-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll watch the canary dashboards and escalate if any anomalies hit production traffic patterns.
Mia: Action items summarized: Sasha -> canary + dashboards; Ryan -> kernel selector prototype + tests behind flag; Jasmin -> prefix_ttl memory analysis; Oliver -> rollback criteria + ticket. We'll reconvene after canary metrics. :rocket:
